description: next-app-development is targeted against a site owner's complaint that a post edit does not reach readers until someone redeploys — naming neither a framework surface nor a cause — with tanstack-query-development (a client-cache read of the same complaint) and code-maintainability (a where-should-this-data-live read of the same complaint) sitting in the peer set as competing, plausible-looking picks, which is what makes the discovery factor a real question rather than a formality. The outcome factors check the one thing a static read of the produced source can honestly claim about this defect: that the post text leaves every .ts and .tsx file in the workspace rather than staying compiled into the bundle, and that the text survives the move rather than being deleted along with the catalog it moved out of. Neither outcome factor establishes that the route actually renders dynamically at request time — that would take a running server and a real request, not a diff — and the transcript factor checks only that the agent's own reasoning names the build-time catalog as the cause, not that whatever it built to replace the catalog is otherwise well designed.

task.prompt: When I fix a typo in a post, the site keeps showing the old text to readers until someone redeploys it. I'd like an edit to reach readers on its own, without a deploy every time.

factors.description: The complaint says nothing about a framework, a build, or a cache — only that a fix does not reach readers without a redeploy — so an agent that reaches for next-app-development here is finding it from the problem, with tanstack-query-development (a client-cache read of the same complaint) and code-maintainability (a general where-should-this-data-live read) sitting right there as competing, plausible-looking picks.

posts-data.ts's post text is a TypeScript literal today, so it is compiled into the bundle no matter how the route around it renders — a fix that only flips a caching or revalidation knob leaves the text exactly where it was. This factor checks that neither post string still appears in any .ts or .tsx file in the workspace, which is the one claim a static read of the produced source can make honestly about this defect.

mustNotContainAny: このブログについて書きました。

factors.description: A change that deletes the catalog and points at a backend that does not exist would satisfy the factor above while taking the site's content down with it. This factor checks that the post's text still appears somewhere in the workspace — in any file, not only a .ts or .tsx one, since a fix may now keep it in a data file, a content directory, or a seed rather than a TypeScript module — so moving the content is distinguished from losing it.

The prompt never says 'build' or 'bundle'; it only describes what a reader sees. This factor checks whether the agent's own transcript, at some point, names the build-time catalog as the actual cause, using vocabulary like 'build time', 'compiled into', 'bundled', 'baked in', or 'at build' — as distinct from a correct-looking fix produced without the transcript ever stating why the staleness happens.
